SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a best-in-class franchise with a durable competitive moat — ~5,000 company-operated stores, 49% gross margins, pricing power, and repeat-demand characteristics. Q1 2026 results confirmed continued execution: revenue +6.8% YoY to $5.67B, EPS +7.5% YoY to $2.15, beating consensus ($2.27 adjusted). The company returned $773M to shareholders in Q1 while maintaining net debt/EBITDA at 2.5x. However, the near-term setup is complicated by three headwinds: (1) the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.45% exceeds the 3.3% earnings yield, creating a persistent valuation drag; (2) WTI crude at $91.58/bbl pressures petrochemical input costs; and (3) management itself expects 'little to no recovery in most end markets' and UBS downgraded to Neutral on 2026-06-02 citing no clear medium-term catalyst. The trailing P/E of 30.2x is near the bottom of its 365-day range (28.0–37.1x), which is mildly supportive, but a 30x multiple on mid-single-digit EPS growth with 2.1x leverage in a 4.45% rate environment is not a compelling value signal — it is arguably fair. The Q1 seasonal trough means Q2/Q3 should show sequential improvement, but this is expected and likely priced in. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to drive a re-rating. Net: a high-quality compounder repricing toward fair value in a hostile macro — not an opportunity, not a short.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue $5.67B (+6.8% YoY), EPS $2.15 (+7.5% YoY), beat consensus of $2.27 adjusted
Gross margin stable at ~49% across four quarters; operating margin 12.0% in Q1 (seasonal trough)
Trailing P/E 30.2x near bottom of 365-day range (28.0–37.1x), but 3.3% earnings yield below 4.45% 10Y Treasury
Debt-to-equity 2.10x ($9.32B debt / $4.43B equity); net debt/EBITDA 2.5x — elevated but deleveraging
Management reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance $11.50–$11.90 but expects 'little to no recovery in most end markets'
UBS downgraded to Neutral on 2026-06-02, cut PT to $330 from $385, citing no clear medium-term catalyst
WTI crude at $91.58/bbl creating ongoing input-cost pressure for petrochemical-derived coatings
Q1 OCF of $139.1M improved from Q1 2025's -$61.1M but thin vs $534.7M net income (seasonal working capital build)
~5,000 company-operated stores provide structural distribution moat; share-gain posture in 4th consecutive down-market year
Potential M&A optionality from AkzoNobel–Axalta merger asset divestitures, but could increase leverage further
